steps.body:
HOME COURTYARD
The patched porch and stacked wood make this place easy to recognize from the lane. The dispatcher is taking runners inside the courier hall on the eastern street.

[E] Continue

ROUTE TABLE
The small table holds a folded map and room for your field notes.

FIRST ROUTE  /  Speak to the dispatcher
ROUTE BOARD  /  Assignment open

[E] Continue

REST CORNER
A teal quilt covers the bed. A small cabinet and woven mat keep this corner separate from the working floor.

[E] Continue

HOME STOVE
An iron stove rests beside a stack of split wood. The clear center floor leaves room to pass between it and the worktable.

[E] Continue

TRAVEL HOOK
A working coat and spare boots are kept beside the doorway.

[E] Continue

SHARED GARDEN
Keep to the aisles around and between the timber beds. The neighbor beside the northern aisle has spare cuttings for the open bed on the right.

[E] Continue

OPEN GARDEN BED
The right bed has room for three rows. The neighbor beside the northern aisle has the shared cuttings; speak to them before planting.

[E] Continue

GARDEN NEIGHBOR
The left bed is planted. We left the right bed open for these spare cuttings. You can plant them from the southern aisle; keep your feet out of the beds.

[E] Continue

SHARED CUTTINGS
You place the spare cuttings in three spaced rows. Both timber beds are planted now, and the aisles around them are clear.

[E] Continue

SHARED CUTTINGS
Three fresh rows fill the right bed. The cuttings are still small, with open soil between them. The walking aisles remain clear.

[E] Continue

GARDEN NEIGHBOR
Those three rows are in. The new cuttings are easy to see against the open soil. Thanks for helping, and keep to the aisles while they settle.

[E] Continue

COURIER BOARD
FIRST ROUTE  /  Speak to the dispatcher
ROUTE BOARD  /  Assignment open

[E] Continue

SORTING SHELVES
Tied canvas bags are arranged beside the counter. Your sealed route pouch stays closed; the dispatcher handles the assignment.

[E] Continue

DISPATCHER
Take this sealed pouch along the river bend to the old ferry relay post. Check whether anyone is keeping the return mark. Leave the seal intact.

[E] Continue

DISPATCH LANE
The courier hall stands beside the eastern street. Follow the Route 1 sign to the opening at the end of that street. Beyond the entrance, the meadow path bends toward the raised levee and river bridge. The courtyard streets return to your home.

[E] Continue

ROUTE 1
The crest road follows the river to the bridge. The old landing and relay post lie along the side path. Keep to the worn track on the raised earth.

[E] Continue

OLD LANDING FOOTPATH
The bank trail passes the height post, then follows lower ground south to the relay and old tieoffs. A second worn track returns to the bridge road. The crest is higher ground. Worn rope grooves mark the older crossing; the cuts on the height post have no dates.

[E] Continue

You slide the sealed pouch into the dry slot. No keeper answers. Today's return mark is missing, but the delivery counts.

[E] Continue

CITY COURIER
Welcome across the river. I have recorded your arrival at this branch. Bring your landing report back to the hometown dispatcher when you are ready. The direction board marks the streets into the city.

[E] Continue

CITY ROUTES
This riverfront branch marks your arrival in the city. The brick frontage and records house are local landmarks. The marked northern lane reaches the historic street, with its repaired shop, public ledger and courier board. The works, school and trade quarters will have separate entrances as they are built. Return west over the bridge for Route 1 and the hometown.

[E] Continue

CITY ADDRESS CHECK
The branch has two address labels for the repaired shop. Compare the old doorway number with the public street ledger, then take the current address back to the city courier.

[E] Continue

REPAIR WORKSHOP
Tools hang in the display windows beneath a worn awning. The keeper is outside, within speaking distance of the doorway.

[E] Continue

WORKSHOP KEEPER
These buildings get new fittings without losing their old doorways. If a parcel label and a lintel disagree, the public ledger across the street has today's address.

[E] Continue

RESIDENTIAL DOORSTEP
A small notice asks delivery runners to knock at each ground-floor door. The separate upstairs curtains and repaired thresholds show that the old row is still lived in.

[E] Continue

PUBLIC STREET LEDGER
Old doorway 6 and current street address 18 refer to the same shop. The street was renumbered; the old lintel was kept. Use 18 for a current courier handoff.

[E] Continue

REPAIRED SHOP
The doorway lintel still carries 6. The new sign above the awning reads 18. The brick frontage is older than this shop's fittings; check the public ledger before choosing a route label.

[E] Continue

WORKSHOP KEEPER
You have both versions now. Take the current street address to the courier at the riverfront branch; the older lintel can stay where it is.

[E] Continue

WORKSHOP KEEPER
The shop route is marked eighteen now. A new fitting is useful, but you do not have to tear out the old stone to keep the street working.

[E] Continue

The marker was turned toward the riverbank. You set its three-dot sign straight and check the ground around its foot.

[E] Continue

SHARED GARDEN
Both timber beds hold cuttings now. Keep to the aisles around and between the beds. The garden neighbor is beside the northern aisle.

[E] Continue

GARDEN NEIGHBOR
Those three rows are in. The new cuttings are easy to see against the open soil. Thanks for helping, and keep to the aisles while they settle.

[E] Continue

SHARED CUTTINGS
Three fresh rows fill the right bed. The cuttings are still small, with open soil between them. The walking aisles remain clear.

[E] Continue

SHARED CUTTINGS
Three fresh rows fill the right bed. The cuttings are still small, with open soil between them. The walking aisles remain clear.

[E] Continue

GARDEN NEIGHBOR
Those three rows are in. The new cuttings are easy to see against the open soil. Thanks for helping, and keep to the aisles while they settle.

[E] Continue

ROUTE TABLE
The route report has been filed. The folded map stays ready for the next trip.

FIRST ROUTE COMPLETE  /  Delivery and report recorded
ROUTE BOARD  /  Empty post

[E] Continue

REST CORNER
A teal quilt covers the bed. A small cabinet and woven mat keep this corner separate from the working floor.

[E] Continue

HOME STOVE
An iron stove rests beside a stack of split wood. The clear center floor leaves room to pass between it and the worktable.

[E] Continue

TRAVEL HOOK
A working coat and spare boots are kept beside the doorway. Your carried route pouch stays with you.

[E] Continue
